channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler zero-days exploited for weeks before disclosure, CISA warns
item.description: Two Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, are under global exploitation, and researchers say intruders were inside appliances for weeks before Citrix disclosed on 27 September. One is an unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw; the other is a memory overflow on DTLS-enabled devices. Dozens of organizations are affected, a public proof of concept exists, and on 1 October LevelBlue detailed a post-exploitation script that creates privileged accounts, exfiltrates configuration data and plants web shells disguised as CSS files. Both flaws are in CISA KEV and the federal deadline has passed. Patching does not evict an intruder. NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, so any unhunted appliance is a possible foothold toward OT. - Citrix security bulletin CTX697096; CISA KEV catalog and 27 Sep alert (30 Sep deadline); Dutch NCSC; Tenable, Rapid7 and watchTowr research; Palo Alto Unit 42 threat brief (28 Sep); reported by The Hacker News (1 Oct, LevelBlue findings), Help Net Security (incl. 29 Sep escalation report), The Hacker News (30 Sep, incl. Mandiant/GTIG WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT findings), BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek - LevelBlue post-exploitation analysis of CVE-2026-88771 attacks (web shells, privileged accounts, config exfiltration) reported 1 Oct 2026 (The Hacker News); Mandiant/GTIG trace CVE-2026-88772 exploitation to early September, suspected state-linked actors (Help Net Security, 30 Sep 2026); public PoC for CVE-2026-88772 and exploitation of it reported 30 Sep 2026; now in mass exploitation (29 Sep 2026); exploited for weeks before disclosure; Citrix confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026; watchTowr technical write-up 28 Sep 2026; escalation to mass exploitation reported 29 Sep 2026; added to CISA KEV 27 Sep 2026 (federal deadline 30 Sep 2026)

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no new development since disclosure
item.description: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote alarms and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It remains the only confirmed case of OT tampering in this edition, with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure. - Colorado Governor’s office statement, reported by Industrial Cyber, Axios Denver and SecurityWeek - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of this edition

item.title: [Medium] Spain’s Adif web systems served as the way into Renfe in a data breach, with no train disruption reported
item.category: Incident — Spanish rail infrastructure manager Adif and operator Renfe hit by a data breach through Adif’s public web infrastructure; passenger data exposed; signalling and train control reported unaffected; attacker unidentified
item.description: Industrial Cyber, citing analysis from Shieldworkz, reports that attackers compromised Adif’s internet-facing web infrastructure after weeks of probing, then pivoted into connected Renfe IT systems and took roughly 500 GB of enterprise data. Adif detected abnormal behavior on 24 September and took its web services offline on 25 September as a precaution; Renfe acknowledged that passenger names and email addresses were exposed, and systems were restored on 26 September. The analysts say signalling, interlocking, traffic control and traction-power systems stayed isolated and untouched. They also describe automated, AI-assisted tooling in the data theft, but could not attribute the activity to any actor. The lesson for rail and transit OT teams is that a shared external web front end can become the bridge between two organizations’ IT networks. - Shieldworkz analysis, reported by Industrial Cyber - Detected 24 Sep 2026; disclosed 25 Sep 2026; systems restored 26 Sep 2026; analysis reported 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] A third vessel’s hijacked-valve claim stays unverified as a Texas regulator urges operators to harden defenses
item.category: Incident — Coast Guard- and FBI-confirmed cyber intrusions on two Galveston-bound tankers boarded in August; a third vessel’s (LNG carrier) crew claim of a hijacked safety system unverified by any maritime authority; a Texas regulator cites the boardings in a public statement; no confirmed shore-side disruption
item.description: The Coast Guard and FBI boarded the tanker VL Prosperity off Galveston on 21 August and a second US-bound tanker on 24 August, with Rear Admiral Amy Grable confirming investigators found evidence of a malicious cyber actor on the vessels’ IT and other onboard systems; neither ship was found unsafe to operate, and the Coast Guard has not publicly attributed the intrusions to Iran despite Iranian state media claiming credit. A third vessel, the LNG carrier Vivit Africa, reported a suspected cyberattack near the Strait of Gibraltar in September; its crew alleged attackers briefly took control of tank-pressure and relief-valve systems, but the Italian Coast Guard and Korean Register have confirmed only a systems malfunction, not a cyberattack. On 24 September, Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a public statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to strengthen their cyber defenses. - US Coast Guard and FBI statements, reported by SecurityWeek and CBS News; Cybernews reporting on the Vivit Africa claim; Railroad Commission of Texas statement via WorldOil - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; Vivit Africa claim reported 21 Sep, updated 24 Sep; Texas statement 24 Sep 2026 — no official development since

item.title: [Medium] Boston Scientific’s worldwide production halt shows how IT-side damage can stop plants without touching controls
item.category: Incident — Boston Scientific halted manufacturing, order processing and shipping worldwide after an August attack that entered through an external-facing network device; investigators reportedly found no compromise of SCADA or plant-maintenance systems; production restored 9 Sep
item.description: An Industrial Cyber analysis published 30 September revisits the attack on medical-device maker Boston Scientific, detected on 25 August. Per that account, CrowdStrike’s investigation found attackers entered through an external-facing network device and reached a limited set of IT systems, with no evidence that SCADA or manufacturing maintenance systems were compromised. Even so, manufacturing, order processing and shipping were disrupted worldwide until systems were restored on 9 September. The lesson for plant defenders is dependency, not intrusion depth: when ERP, ordering and logistics systems go down, the plant stops even if the control network is clean. - Industrial Cyber expert analysis (30 Sep 2026), citing company disclosures and CrowdStrike’s investigation - Attack 25 Aug 2026; systems restored 9 Sep 2026; investigation findings reported 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Chained flaws in an IO-Link master hand an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor data
item.category: Research — CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014: 18 CVEs across Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3 IO-Link masters, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass and a persistent command-injection flaw; chainable for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation
item.description: CERT@VDE disclosed 18 vulnerabilities in Pepperl+Fuchs’s ICE2 and ICE3 series IO-Link masters on 16 September in advisory VDE-2026-014. The worst, CVE-2026-27546, is an authentication bypass scored CVSS 9.8; a companion flaw, CVE-2026-27565, lets an attacker inject operating-system commands through a malicious IODD file upload that persists after reboot. Chained together, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. Nozomi Networks’ 29 September write-up counts 19 flaws in the ICE2 model and says two HTTPS requests are enough to take root. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover. - CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014 - Published 16 Sep 2026; Nozomi technical write-up 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Ransomware volume hit a 2026 high in August, and industrial organizations took roughly a third of it
item.category: Threat intel — NCC Group’s August 2026 ransomware review counts 1,073 attacks, up 12% on July, with the industrial sector the target in about 31%; Qilin leads; no CVE
item.description: NCC Group’s review of August 2026, reported by Industrial Cyber on 28 September, recorded 1,073 ransomware attacks, a 12% rise on July. Industrial organizations were the target in 329 of them (31%), and North America took 44% of all victims. Qilin was the most active operator with 164 incidents (15%), overtaking The Gentlemen. The report also flags Aurora, a ransomware-as-a-service group active since late April that goes after manufacturing and transport using VPN exploitation, credential harvesting and hypervisor encryption — the same remote-access edge covered elsewhere in this edition. These are victim-leak-site counts, so they measure claimed attacks rather than confirmed operational shutdowns. - NCC Group monthly threat report, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 28 Sep 2026; covers August 2026 activity

item.title: [Medium] One malformed packet can crash TDengine, a database behind industrial telemetry and monitoring
item.category: Research — Ridge Security disclosure of CVE-2026-42542 (CVSS 7.5), a pre-authentication denial-of-service flaw in the TDengine time-series database used for industrial telemetry; fixed in 3.4.1.6; no known exploitation
item.description: Ridge Security reported on 25 September an integer-underflow bug in how TDengine parses messages before authentication. A single malformed packet sent to TCP port 6030 can crash an affected instance (versions 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5). TDengine is a time-series database common in industrial, IoT, energy and automotive monitoring, so a crash can blind historians and dashboards rather than stop a process. The vendor published its advisory in June and patches have been available since April; the researchers have not released their proof-of-concept, but say the bug is relatively easy to reproduce. We tag it Medium because it is availability-only and not known to be exploited. - Ridge Security research, reported by Industrial Cyber and Dark Reading - Research reported 25 Sep 2026 (Dark Reading 28 Sep); vendor fix and advisory predate it (patch available since April, advisory 4 Jun)

item.title: [Critical] Check Point’s federal patch deadline has passed for two exploited flaws spanning the VPN gateway and the server that manages it
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway/Spark VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers/SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed
item.description: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two separate flaws now past their federal remediation deadline. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation issue on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal affecting Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September alongside flaws in Arista VeloCloud and F5 BIG-IP APM; the 25 September deadline has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small, unmanned sites. - Check Point security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer and Help Net Security - Exploitation confirmed by 22 Sep 2026; KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

item.title: [High] F5 BIG-IP APM zero-day: unauthenticated code execution on OAuth servers, exploited and past its federal deadline
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-94127, F5 BIG-IP APM configured as an OAuth authorization server; heap overflow, unauthenticated remote code execution (CVSS 9.8 v3.1); exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed
item.description: F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 on 22 September: a heap-based buffer overflow in BIG-IP Access Policy Manager that gives an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution when APM is set up as an OAuth authorization server. Systems using APM only as a client or resource server are not affected. The flaw is being exploited, CISA added it to KEV the same day, and the 25 September federal deadline has passed. BIG-IP appliances commonly front remote-access and vendor portals into industrial networks, so an exposed one is a path toward OT even though it runs no control loop. - F5 security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; reported by The Hacker News - F5 advisory and KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

item.title: [High] Cisco warns of a fifth SD-WAN zero-day this year: an authentication bypass in SD-WAN Manager is being exploited
item.category: Advisory — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-76504) exploited in the wild; fixed releases available; added to CISA KEV 30 Sep 2026 with a 3 Oct federal deadline; exploiting actor not named
item.description: Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504, a flaw in how Catalyst SD-WAN Manager handles URI encoding in HTTP requests, lets an attacker bypass authentication on the API session layer and gain administrator access. Cisco says it is already being exploited, without naming an actor, and CISA added it to the KEV catalog the same day with a 3 October federal deadline. Fixed releases exist for each supported train. Reporting counts it as the fifth SD-WAN zero-day exploited in 2026. In our assessment (editorial, not from the source), SD-WAN managers often control the WAN links that tie remote substations, plants and pipeline sites back to headquarters, so administrator takeover is a path toward those sites. - Cisco advisory as reported by BleepingComputer; CISA KEV catalog - Disclosed and added to KEV 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A broken authentication check in Schneider’s flagship M580 safety PLC needs a validated patch window
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-3869 (CVSS v4 9.2), Schneider Electric Modicon M580, M580 Safety and MC80 PLCs; incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm; fixed firmware available (SEVD-2026-251-04), no known exploitation
item.description: Schneider Electric disclosed CVE-2026-3869 on 9 September in advisory SEVD-2026-251-04: an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm affecting Modicon M580 controllers below application level 4.00, M580 Safety below 4.20, and Modicon MC80 units. The flaw scores CVSS v4 9.2 and could let an attacker who reaches the controller bypass authentication on management functions. The M580 is Schneider’s flagship PLC platform, deployed widely across process manufacturing, water, oil and gas and power applications, and the Safety variant runs safety-instrumented functions tied directly to process protection. No exploitation has been reported, and fixed firmware is available, but like most safety-certified controllers it can’t be patched without a validated change-control cycle, so unpatched units are likely to stay in service for weeks or months — making network isolation the interim control that matters most. - Schneider Electric advisory SEVD-2026-251-04; CVE-2026-3869 public record - Published 9 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A critical bug in the lwIP network stack embedded in countless controllers and gateways lets an attacker run code remotely
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-265-01: out-of-bounds write in the lwIP embedded TCP/IP stack’s MQTT client, CVE-2026-87121, CVSS 9.8; public proof-of-concept reported; not in CISA KEV
item.description: CISA published advisory ICSA-26-265-01 on 22 September for CVE-2026-87121 (CVSS 9.8), an out-of-bounds write in the MQTT client component of lwIP, a widely embedded open-source TCP/IP stack. An unauthenticated network attacker could gain code execution on a device that uses the vulnerable MQTT client. Because lwIP ships inside many vendors’ firmware, exposure depends on whether a given product enables the MQTT client and which vendor has issued a rebuilt image. A public proof-of-concept has been reported, but the flaw is not in CISA’s exploited-vulnerabilities catalog and no in-the-wild use is confirmed. Asset owners will mostly be waiting on their device vendors. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-265-01; corroborated by CVE record aggregators - Advisory published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] TeamViewer urges immediate updates for five flaws, including a session-control bypass that could lead to code execution
item.category: Advisory — TeamViewer Full Client and Host: five vulnerabilities including a remote-session access-control bypass that could lead to code execution (CVE-2026-92370); fixed in 15.82; vendor reports no known exploitation; CVSS not published in the source
item.description: TeamViewer released version 15.82 on 30 September to fix five vulnerabilities in its Windows, Linux and macOS clients and hosts. The most serious, CVE-2026-92370, is a remote-session access-control bypass that could allow unauthorized actions up to remote code execution; the others are a path traversal, a heap buffer overflow, a race condition and a path-validation error. TeamViewer says it is not aware of public disclosure or exploitation in the wild, and the reporting gives no CVSS scores. The product is not OT-specific, but it is a common vendor and technician remote-access tool on engineering workstations and HMIs, so any copy reaching plant networks deserves attention. Severity here is an editorial estimate. - TeamViewer advisory as reported by BleepingComputer - Published 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] GAO: overlapping federal incident-reporting rules burden critical infrastructure operators
item.category: Policy — GAO report on overlapping federal cyber-incident reporting rules affecting critical infrastructure operators; no CVE
item.description: A Government Accountability Office report released on 1 October found that operators in sectors including energy, financial services and healthcare face conflicting and duplicative federal and sector-specific cyber-incident reporting requirements. Industry participants proposed harmonizing timeframes, thresholds and definitions, naming a single lead agency such as CISA to receive and share reports, and expanding government-industry collaboration. About half of participants said progress over the past year has been limited. For OT operators, the practical effect is that one incident can trigger several reporting clocks at once. - US Government Accountability Office; reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Cyber threat-sharing law gets a short extension to 11 December, not a permanent fix
item.category: Policy — temporary extension of the federal cyber threat-information sharing law; forward-looking sunset date; no CVE
item.description: A stopgap funding bill passed by the House pushes the sunset of the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 from 30 September to 11 December 2026; reporting on 1 September said the President was expected to sign it. The law shields companies from lawsuits and regulatory penalties when they voluntarily share threat data with agencies such as CISA. Industry groups have warned that a lapse would make operators hesitant to report intrusions, and repeated attempts at long-term reauthorization have stalled. Utilities and manufacturers that feed incident data to their ISACs and CISA should expect the question to come back before year end. - Defense One; also reported by Nextgov/FCW and Federal News Network - Reported 1 Sep 2026; extended sunset 11 Dec 2026 (forward-looking)

item.title: [Info] FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
item.category: Guidance — FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion
item.description: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk on 24 September, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. The agencies say intruders searched the company’s systems for terms like “customers” and “SCADA” and staged customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; downstream customers referenced in the guidance include power utilities and transportation entities. The guidance recommends least-privilege integrator access, on-demand and auditable remote sessions, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security terms in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if an integrator is compromised. - FBI and CISA joint fact sheet; reported by Industrial Cyber - Released 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — comments are open until 30 November
item.category: Guidance — NIST releases initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security”; expanded sector scope, restructured around CSF 2.0; comment period through 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail and maritime vessels; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026, and it lands the same week as the FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above). - NIST Computer Security Resource Center; reported by SecurityWeek and Industrial Cyber - Draft published 21 Sep 2026; comments due 30 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Australia’s CISC shifts from partnership to tiered enforcement of critical-infrastructure security duties
item.category: Regulation — Australia’s CISC moves to tiered SOCI Act enforcement from the 2026–27 financial year; no CVE
item.description: Australia’s Critical Infrastructure Security Centre says it will enforce the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SOCI) Act through three escalating steps: guidance notices for gaps below the non-compliance threshold, formal non-compliance notices, and infringement notices for serious or persistent breaches. The approach takes effect in the 2026–27 financial year and follows the 2026 independent review of the Act. It applies to all regulated entities, including energy, water, transport and other operators with OT, and weighs factors such as severity, conduct, harm and whether an issue was self-reported. - Australian CISC announcement; reported by Industrial Cyber - Reported 29 Sep 2026; applies 2026–27 financial year
